pass_a_gloss: clouds also ran with dews. Earth named in this place holy Paul termed breadth; what here are named heavens he in the Epistle to the Ephesians terms height; abysses tropically so called he terms depth; clouds wet with dew he terms length. These are all tokens of rational natures portioned among worlds and body after the proportion of their condition. The same now also suits the Son of God. Yet the believing soul is earth yielding a hundredfold as well; she grows wise from that wealth which is wisdom, God setting her foundation on it. He plants the assembly of teaching and fashions a bond out of wisdom; and while she keeps advancing he turns her into heaven — most pure creature, home of angels and of noetic beings — once she has taken sense of beings and looks on the precision of things as if on Gods multi-story judgments. Demons have no force against wisdom alone; they may not throw thoughts into the heart of one made wise, since a mind racing after wisdoms contemplations becomes closed to unclean thoughts. A clean mind approaches wisdom for it knows the good; an unclean mind stays distant from her. For rational nature a trip-stone is unclean thought or spurious knowledge; yet one hedged by counsel of God does not trip in these. An onset of wicked thoughts, he says, will not scare the person who has become wise, nor will the impious who strike from outside pull down his strength when they aim to rob him of natural goods — nobody can seize what is unseizable — and what pride exceeds that of the impious? Still you will conquer that many-shaped beast too if you are mild and fair, the Lord being with you. Hence we learn mercy drives off fearful phantasms meeting us by night, or also in contemplation; and beyond that it clears from such minds the wicked charges at departure and the damaging chastisements at judgment. Mildness, freedom from anger, patience, and whatever calms stirred wrath by nature do likewise, if fearful sights usually spring from wraths turmoil. Do not hold back from benefiting — not only with food for the needy but also with knowledge of God and wisdom and commands; and whatever is dear to God and joins one to him, do not hold back from benefiting the one who needs you. Hatred toward the neighbor makes a person evil in body and also in soul. Ignorance of the Lord dwells in houses of the impious, knowledge of God in souls of the just; houses of the just are blessed when Christ assigns prizes to each by their works; for the impious a curse, not a blessing. Vice pushed to its tip is named pride; the Lord sets himself against the unjust as righteousness, against liars as truth, against the proud as humility; so he is friend to those who think humble things — He gives grace to the humble — and against the proud he sets himself. Learners and teachers of godly wisdom will inherit heavenly glory; the impious raised dishonor for themselves before angels and humans from Christ. Training means ethical virtue; thought means divine knowledge; a son of the virtues is one fitted by them who acts not for anothers sake but for virtues sake in what fits it. I grant you a good gift, the heavenly kingdom, if you do not leave my law; note he names the mind a good gift, because of one who takes gifts unjustly in the bosom and is not prospered; those unjust gifts are the evil ones affairs, and a mind receiving them is not prospered in its ways. Crown of graces = Gods commands, which return the kingdoms crown to those who do them; crown of delight = knowledge of God, which as a shield thrusts off every passionate thought and every false knowledge. These many ways run into one way — the one who said I am the way; many ways he named the virtues that carry to knowledge of God. Years of life for the hearer through the prophets of the heavenly Father will increase, and for the one receiving his words through the only-begotten Son, to be steered in ways of righteousness of life so as to be saved into ever-living life. Of this

and the clouds ran with dews. So the “earth” he named here, holy Paul called breadth; and what are called heavens here, Paul in Ephesians calls height; and the abysses named in a figure he calls depth; the dewed clouds he calls length. All of these are symbols of rational natures, divided among worlds and body according to the analogy of their state. This also fits the Son of God now. But the faithful soul is also earth that bears a hundredfold. From the richness that is wisdom she becomes wise, while God founds her upon it. For he settles the gathering of teaching and makes a fastening from wisdom. And as she always advances, he makes her heaven—a purest creature, a dwelling of angels and of noetic essences—once she has received sense of what is and contemplates the exactness of things, as if the many-storied judgments of God.

Against wisdom alone the demons are powerless. They are not allowed to cast thoughts into the heart of the one who has been made wise. For the mind that competes for the contemplations of wisdom becomes unreceptive of unclean thoughts. A pure mind draws near to wisdom, because it knows the good; the unclean mind will be far from her. A stumbling-block for a rational nature is an unclean thought or false knowledge. But the one fenced round by God’s counsel does not stumble in these things.

Neither an assault of wicked thoughts, he says, will frighten the one who has become wise, nor will the impious who attack from outside tear down his power when they want to strip him of natural goods. No one can take what cannot be captured—and what is more arrogant than the impious person? Yet you will also overcome that many-formed beast if you are gentle and equitable, while the Lord is with you. From this we learn that mercy removes the fearful phantasms that meet us by night, or also in contemplation. And not only that: it also removes from those who think this way the wicked accusations at the departure and the harmful chastisements in the judgment. Gentleness, freedom from anger, long-suffering, and whatever naturally settles stirred wrath do the same—if fearful appearances usually arise from the turmoil of wrath.

Do not hold back from doing good not only with food for the needy, but also with the knowledge of God, with wisdom, and with the commandments. And whatever is dear to God and joins a person to him, do not hold back from doing that good to the one who needs you. This enmity toward the neighbor makes someone evil not only in body but also in soul. Ignorance of the Lord is in the houses of the impious, but knowledge of God is in the souls of the just. The dwellings of the just are blessed when Christ apportions the prizes to each according to their works; to the impious he apportions a curse and not a blessing.

Extreme vice raised to its end is called pride. The Lord arrays himself against the unjust as righteousness, against liars as truth, against the proud as humility. That is why he is a friend to those who think humble thoughts—for that is what “He gives grace to the humble” means—and against the proud he arrays himself. Those who have learned and taught godly wisdom will inherit heavenly glory. The impious raised dishonor for themselves before angels and human beings from Christ.

By “training” he means ethical virtue; by “thought,” divine knowledge. A “son of the virtues” is the one qualified according to them, who acts not for someone else’s sake but for virtue’s sake in what accords with it. “I grant you a good gift, the heavenly kingdom, if you do not abandon my law.” Note here that he names the mind a good gift, because of the one who takes gifts unjustly in the bosom and is not prospered. Those unjust gifts mean the affairs of the evil one; when the mind receives them, it is not prospered in its ways.

A crown of graces are God’s commandments, which give back the crown of the kingdom to those who do them. A crown of delight is the knowledge of God, which shields us and thrusts away every passionate thought and every false knowledge. These many ways lead into one way—the one who said, “I am the way.” He called many ways the virtues that carry a person to the knowledge of God. The years of life of the one who hears through the prophets of the heavenly Father will be multiplied, and who receives his words through the only-begotten Son, so as to be directed in the ways of righteousness of life and saved into the ever-living life. Of this
